title: Make authentication retries redirect to a new channel
body: We can simplify nsHttpChannel quite a bit if we make the authentication retry not use the same nsHttpChannel but instead to an internal redirect to the same URL with the proper credentials.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hey Luca,

With our new implementation, on authentication failures we would send the retry requests with auth headers on the new 
(redirected) channel.  
Hence, we will be sending the "http-on-modify-request" and "http-on-before-connect" observer notifications for the new channel before sending the request instead of the old channel which received the auth failure status. 

We would like to know if this would have any impacts on the webextensions? 

Thanks

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hey Rob,
With my changes, we have changed the mechanism of  process auth failures (401/407).

Instead of sending the request with authentication information from the same channel we do internal redirect and send the request with authentication information from the new channel. You can find a detailed description about the design [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19rOsVC8n3td_wqffboim3c710LgVAaVF1YZDycskmWo/edit) 

Unfortunately, there are some impacts on webextensions due to my changes. 

We see that [test_webRequest_duelingAuth](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/toolkit/components/extensions/test/xpcshell/test_ext_webRequest_auth.js#308) test fails primarily due to the following exception
```
 0:01.48 pid:3475 JavaScript error: resource://gre/modules/WebRequest.sys.mjs, line 1213: NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED
```
The reason for this exception is that [nsHttpChannel::Resume](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp#5793) returns `NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED`. 
From Necko logs, I could see that the `WebRequest.sys.mjs` script  is [suspending](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#1066) the channel when prompting for auth credentials. On generation of credentials Necko  redirects to the new channel.
The script later calls [resume](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#1217) on the redirected channel. 
Hence, [this](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp#5794) check in nsHttpChannel fails as the redirected channel was never suspended.


I would need your help in understanding if there are any additional notification you would expect such that the we don't call resume on the redirected channel?
Please let me know if you need any additional logs.
Thank you in advance.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
(In reply to comment #6)
> With our new implementation, on authentication failures we would send the retry requests with auth headers on the new 
> (redirected) channel.  
> Hence, we will be sending the "http-on-modify-request" and "http-on-before-connect" observer notifications for the new channel before sending the request instead of the old channel which received the auth failure status. 
> 
> We would like to know if this would have any impacts on the webextensions? 

As described, the changes may potentially affects the following parts of the API:

- webRequest.onAuthRequired, dispatched by [`asyncPromptAuth` handler](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/fb43eb3bdf5b51000bc7dfe3474cbe56ca2ab63c/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#504,559) registered at `http-on-examine-response`
- webRequest.onBeforeRequest = "http-on-modify-request".
- webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders = "http-on-before-connect"

I haven't tested your patch yet, but I did compare the behavior of Firefox and Chrome (and the documentation on MDN and Chrome's developer docs). These four all differ from each other, unfortunately. I described the behavior in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1847637 along with an extension and instructions to test manually. Give it a try with your patch and show the output if you have questions on the validity of the extension-observed behavior.

(In reply to comment #8)
> Hey Rob,
> With my changes, we have changed the mechanism of  process auth failures (401/407).
> 
> Instead of sending the request with authentication information from the same channel we do internal redirect and send the request with authentication information from the new channel. You can find a detailed description about the design [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/19rOsVC8n3td_wqffboim3c710LgVAaVF1YZDycskmWo/edit)

Not extension-specific, but relevant question: how does the change interact with the internal redirect loop detection logic in [HttpBaseChannel::CheckRedirectLimit](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/netwerk/protocol/http/HttpBaseChannel.cpp#5851-5873)? Is the extra consumed `mInternalRedirectCount` budget reasonable under normal situations and in edge cases? The main thing I'd like to know is if users may get dangerously close to the (internal) redirect limit, to the point that there is not enough budget left for a reasonably small number of server-side redirects. There are many ways to authenticate, and I am not sufficiently familiar with all authentication mechanisms to tell what happens. For example, NLTM involves multiple challenge-response messages - how many internal redirects are counted?

(meta comment: when linking Searchfox links, please use Permalink from the sidebar so that the link always points to the same code. I have replaced the original links with permalinks in the quote below to make it easier to follow the discussion in the future)

> Unfortunately, there are some impacts on webextensions due to my changes. 
> 
> We see that [test_webRequest_duelingAuth](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/toolkit/components/extensions/test/xpcshell/test_ext_webRequest_auth.js#308) test fails primarily due to the following exception
> ```
>  0:01.48 pid:3475 JavaScript error: resource://gre/modules/WebRequest.sys.mjs, line 1213: NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED
> ```
> The reason for this exception is that [nsHttpChannel::Resume](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp#5793) returns `NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED`. 
> From Necko logs, I could see that the `WebRequest.sys.mjs` script  is [suspending](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#1061) the channel when prompting for auth credentials. On generation of credentials Necko  redirects to the new channel.
> The script later calls [resume](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#1118) on the redirected channel. 
> Hence, [this](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/netwerk/protocol/http/nsHttpChannel.cpp#5794) check in nsHttpChannel fails as the redirected channel was never suspended.

When there is any `webRequest.onAuthRequired` listener, the implementation suspends a channel before an extension has had any chance to respond with credentials, and that's implemented through the [`nsIAuthPrompt2` interface](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/netwerk/base/nsIAuthPrompt2.idl#68-103):

- suspend: [`AuthRequestor`'s `asyncPromptAuth`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#503-573) (the actual `suspend()` call is called by `runChannelListener` - a synchronous method).
- resume: [`applyChanges`'s final part](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#1198,1211-1212) responds with the credentials before calling `resume` (unless the authentication request was already canceled)
  - note `channel.resume()` there is actually handled by [`ChannelWrapper::Resume`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/ChannelWrapper.cpp#271-275), which forwards to the underlying channel.

The WebRequest logic seems correct, so if you're encountering `NS_ERROR_UNEXPECTED` in [the `channel.resume()` call](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/e4d8451468be3a0f8a9faa3d37cadf07200821ec/toolkit/components/extensions/webrequest/WebRequest.sys.mjs#1212), then it means that your patch caused the underlying channel to proceed without accounting for the suspended state. I am not seeing any reference to `mCallOnResume` in your patch, could that be the issue? See the changes in bug 1407384 for example.

> I would need your help in understanding if there are any additional notification you would expect such that the we don't call resume on the redirected channel?

Given the above analysis, I believe that it's not a lack of notification to WebRequest, but a lack of checking the suspended state in the channel.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
(In reply to comment #10)
> By comparing the above events without my patch, I see an additional __onBeforeRedirect__ event that is fired after the user enters the credentials.
> Please let me know if this breaks anything?

It is not documented, but neither is the onAuthRequired > onBeforeRequest transition.

IMO introducing the extra onBeforeRedirect event is acceptable, provided that it's covered by unit tests and documented. Currently, onBeforeRedirect is documented to signal server-side redirects, while in reality it also covers more (internal) redirects. That mismatch in documentation and actual behavior has been raised before in bug 1817450, and IMO an acceptable resolution could be to just document this transition.

The onBeforeRedirect event has additional fields in its details. Are extensions able to discern the different kinds of redirects? Please test all potentially relevant details fields in the unit test.
